scope: Verification of the Layer A event-level decay simulator (src/rnglab/nuclear) against analytic decay laws, with healthy generators only. It is not an RNG-sensitivity experiment, not evidence about branching processes, criticality or detectors, not a test of H1, H2 or H3, and not part of the Stage D pilot. Every nuclide and parameter is synthetic.
seed_recipe: rnglab.seeds.namespace_seed(namespace, run, scheme, 'physics') for every run except ENS; namespace_seed(namespace, 'ENS', 'S2', 'physics', f'{r:04d}') for ensemble replicate r = 0..replicates-1

generators.numpy-pcg64: rnglab.nuclear.NumpyPCG64Source(seed): numpy PCG64 raw 64-bit outputs, seeded with SeedSequence(seed)

engine: rnglab.nuclear.simulate_decays with chunk 65536 unless a run states otherwise

PC1.role: positive control: half-life 2% longer than the reference

PC2.role: positive control: branching 0.62/0.38 against the reference 0.64/0.36

XREF.role: software check: two engines on the same stream

REPLAY.role: software check: replay with another chunk size

T1.what: decay times of Sa-400 against the exponential with rate ln 2 / 1.0 truncated at the horizon

T2.what: Sa-400 count at t against Binomial(N, 2^-t)

T3.what: photons of the Sa-400 channel against Binomial(decays, 0.6)

T4.what: counts in all nine states against Multinomial(N, p(t)), p from the matrix exponential
T4.method: chi-square with the pooling rule (min expected 5)

T5.what: decays of each unstable nuclide within the horizon against Binomial(N, q_j(12)), q from decay_probabilities

T6.what: decays through the first channel against Binomial(decays of the nuclide, first branching ratio)

T7.what: decay times of the nuclide in unit bins against the multinomial law from decay_probabilities
T7.method: chi-square with the pooling rule (min expected 5)

T8.what: photons of each channel whose yield lies strictly between 0 and 1, against Binomial(decays through the channel, yield)

T9.what: counts in the three states against Multinomial(N, p(t))
T9.method: chi-square with the pooling rule (min expected 5)

T10a.what: count of eligible nuclide j at t = 2 summed over replicates against Binomial(replicates * 2000, p_j(2))

T10b.what: between-replicate variance of the count of eligible nuclide j at t = 2 against 2000 p_j (1 - p_j)
T10b.method: (R - 1) s^2 / variance against chi-square(R - 1), two-sided; a normal-theory approximation

tests.eligibility: nuclides with 2000 p_j(2) (1 - p_j(2)) >= 20, from the matrix exponential before generation (design.json)

families.NC1: T1 to T9 on the NC1 runs, and T10a and T10b
families.NC2: T1 to T9 on the NC2 runs

deterministic_checks.D1: every run, including both XREF engines, REPLAY and every ENS replicate, reads exactly nuclei * 3 * depth words, and the source's byte count is 8 times that
deterministic_checks.D2: every run of NC1, NC2, PC1, PC2, XREF and ENS satisfies every rnglab.nuclear.checks.decay_invariants item
deterministic_checks.D3: XREF: identical discrete columns, final states and stream digests in the two engines, and the largest relative time difference at most 1e-12
deterministic_checks.D4: REPLAY: events digest and stream digest equal to those of the NC1 S2 run
deterministic_checks.D5: ENS: 400 distinct seeds and 400 distinct stream digests
deterministic_checks.A1: no random numbers: largest absolute difference between the matrix exponential and the closed-form Bateman path sum at most 1e-11, for every scheme, start nuclide and test time; generator column sums at most 1e-15 in absolute value

reading_rules.R1: Layer A agreement with the analytic laws: PASS iff D1 to D5 and A1 hold and Holm at family-wise alpha 0.01 rejects no test in NC1 and none in NC2. Otherwise FAIL, listing each failed item. A FAIL from one test family with everything else passing is reported as such and is not explained away; the chance of a false FAIL is at most about 2% (two families at 1%).
reading_rules.R2: Sensitivity: PC1 must reject its target test and PC2 its target test, each at p < 0.01 / (size of the NC1 family). If either does not, R1 is reported with the statement that the battery lacked the declared sensitivity.
reading_rules.R3: Descriptive, no verdict: from NC1 S3, the ratio of Yb-410 to Ya-410 decays in (20, 40] with an approximate 95% interval (delta method on the log ratio, with the variances and the covariance of the two per-nucleus window indicators estimated from the run), next to its exact expectation from decay_probabilities and the transient-equilibrium limit lambda_b / (lambda_b - lambda_a).
reading_rules.general: The study runs once from a clean committed tree. Every outcome is reported whichever way it falls. No threshold, size or test changes after generation; a code change after the freeze is an amendment written before any affected number is regenerated.

smoke.output: research/v020-nuclear-a-verify/smoke/ (not in Git, excluded from every result)
